heading: INT. CLOCK TOWER MECHANISM ROOM - NIGHT

units.text: INT. CLOCK TOWER MECHANISM ROOM - NIGHT
Iron gears the size of cartwheels turn behind a dusty rail.

JUNE KOWALCZYK, thirties, a clockmaker in leather gloves, crouches by the main wheel with a lantern while REGGIE FAIRWEATHER, fifties, the town clerk, climbs the last rung of the ladder, wheezing, and drops a folded paper on the floor that June snatches before he can reach it, reads, crumples, and shoves into her pocket as Reggie lunges for her wrist.
Reggie, the hands stopped at 11:42 on the night your brother died.
units.name: JUNE

units.text: Somebody held them there. With a pin through the escapement.
units.name: JUNE

units.text: Reggie backs toward the ladder, hand on the rail, one boot already finding the rung.
June blocks the way, lantern raised, her shadow swelling across the gears.
Both of them look up as the great bell above them begins, slowly, to ring.
